item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 30): "By Design"
item.description: "Sunday Morning" presents its annual edition touching on all aspects of design, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Google updates maps to show "Lake America" in U.S. after Trump order
item.description: Google announced that it had begun rolling out changes to how its maps display Lake Ontario's name, after President Trump signed an executive order changing it to "Lake America."

item.title: The appeal of soft pretzels
item.description: The twisty, crunchy, doughy treat is a tradition in Philadelphia, and the Center City Soft Pretzel Company churns out tens of thousands of pretzels a week. Correspondent Susan Spencer checks out their salty allure. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: Longwood Gardens' jewel of nature
item.description: After industrialist Pierre S. du Pont bought a small farm outside Philadelphia to save its trees from being sold for lumber, he spent the rest of his life creating his dream oasis. Today, the 1,700-acre Longwood Gardens, recently expanded, continues its mission of providing "joy and inspiration to everyone through the beauty of nature, conservation, and learning." Jim Axelrod reports. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: ICE sends Afghans and others to Africa, expanding "third country" deportations
item.description: Over a 10-day period, the Trump administration sent more than 100 deportees from Afghanistan, Cuba and other nations to eight countries across Africa, according to internal government documents obtained by CBS News.

item.title: Extended interview: Louis Vuitton artistic director Nicolas Ghesquière
item.description: In this web exclusive, correspondent Alina Cho talks with Nicolas Ghesquière, artistic director of the French fashion house Louis Vuitton, the world's largest luxury brand.

item.title: Louis Vuitton: Designing the future
item.description: The French fashion house Louis Vuitton, which opened its doors in 1854, is today the world's largest luxury brand. Correspondent Alina Cho talks with artistic director Nicolas Ghesquière, who is shaping the future of Louis Vuitton by designing the unexpected. Cho also gets a sneak preview of Ghesquière's latest collection, as well as a look at a collaboration between LV and the estate of late artist Keith Haring. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: Ferry carrying nearly 270 people capsizes off Cyprus, killing at least 7
item.description: A ferry carrying nearly 270 passengers and crew capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus.

item.title: Philadelphia architect Frank Furness' enduring spirit
item.description: Philadelphia architect Frank Furness, a former Army captain during the Civil War, translated his fearlessness into the designs of about 1,000 buildings – elaborate structures whose oversized arches, asymmetrical facades and eccentric decorations broke free from the polite Victorian era-style. ""Sunday Morning"" national correspondent Robert Costa takes a tour of Furness' Philadelphia with Wall Street Journal architectural critic Michael Lewis, who explains why the architect's reputation has gained a reappraisal. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: Why Philadelphia cheesesteaks rule
item.description: Nothing says love like a Philadelphia cheesesteak sandwich, according to Frankie Olivieri, the third-generation owner of Philly's legendary Pat's King of Steaks. He explains why to correspondent Susan Spencer. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: A spotlight on the glamour of chandeliers
item.description: Mo Rocca sheds light on the traditions of chandeliers, and why these decorative hanging light fixtures can be the star of any room. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: Toppling dominoes as art
item.description: Lily Hevesh may be the world's greatest domino artist. She talked with correspondent David Pogue about the patience and perseverance required to set up thousands of dominoes in intricate structures and patterns – and then knock them all down. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: Ardrossan Mansion: A Philadelphia time capsule
item.description: Jane Pauley takes viewers on a tour of Ardrossan, a 750-acre Georgian-style estate (and an example of Gilded Age-inspired opulence) on Philadelphia's storied Main Line. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: A housing alternative right in your own backyard
item.description: Accessory Dwelling Units, or ADUs, are small, fully-functional secondary homes located on the same property as a main home (usually in the backyard) that serve as carriage houses or "granny flats." But as wildfires have displaced residents in the West, ADUs have filled a vital need where housing has proved scant or expensive. Correspondent Lee Cowan looks at the practical and legal challenges to making ADUs available. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: Philadelphia, the City of Brotherly Love
item.description: Jane Pauley showcases Philadelphia, a city of history and style, which for more than 250 years has been emblematic of our never-ending quest to live better. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: At least 1 killed, 5 injured in shooting at rave in Switzerland
item.description: Local police said early Sunday a manhunt was underway and the motives were still unclear.

item.title: NASA launches its Roman Space Telescope to explore the hidden universe
item.description: NASA's Roman Space Telescope​ launched shortly after daybreak from Kennedy Space Center and blazed toward an observation point 1 million miles away.

item.title: Iran vows to resist U.S. sanctions as war passes 6-month mark
item.description: As the war passes the six-month mark, neither side showed any sign of backing down.

item.title: Roman Space Telescope promises 300-megapixel views of the cosmos
item.description: The $4.3 billion telescope is expected to discover tens of thousands of exoplanets while probing the nature of mysterious dark matter and energy.

item.title: Nepal flash flood death toll reaches 800, with around 3,000 still missing
item.description: Poor weather and challenging terrain have hampered aerial rescue operations in Nepal and Tibet.

item.title: USS Lincoln sails past Singapore after 9-month deployment
item.description: Associated Press journalists on the Indonesian island of Batam, across the Singapore Strait, spotted the massive vessel as it transited waters near Singapore just after 1 a.m. local time.

item.title: Dozens evacuated from Grand Canyon National Park after flash floods
item.description: No injuries were reported but park officials warned people against accessing the closed areas.

item.title: Iceland rejects EU membership talks in referendum vote
item.description: The country is already part of the European Economic Area and the Schengen Area, which allows frictionless movement of people, goods, capital and services.

item.title: Was a police search for a murder weapon cut short by a guard dog's growl?
item.description: After Kevin Davis was found dying at the foot of the stairs in his Indiana home, police initially believed it was an accident. They did not search the room where a pit bull mix was secured.

item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: True crime. Real justice. To miss it would be a crime.

item.title: A wife is accused of her husband's murder. Can she clear her name?
item.description: Alison Davis says she woke up to find her husband, Kevin Davis, face down in a pool of blood inside their New Haven, Indiana, home. She says he fell down the stairs. But after an autopsy report, police came to a different conclusion.

item.title: Trump cannot deport students for criticizing Israel, federal judge rules
item.description: The judge delivered a victory for Stanford University's student newspaper, which said some international students were afraid to speak out because of the deportation threat.

item.title: A Death in the Stairwell
item.description: After her husband is found dying at the foot of the stairs, a woman accused of murder fights to clear her name. "48 Hours" correspondent Peter Van Sant reports.

item.title: Couple recounts surviving deadly Nepal flood: "I knew I was going to die"
item.description: A California couple were in a Nepali village when an avalanche of powerful waters ripped down from the high Himalayas toward them.

item.title: Husband-wife duo team on a mission to race all World Marathon Majors, in hopes of inspiring others
item.description: Amy and Jamie Shinneman plan to run their fifth marathon together in Sydney, Australia, on Aug. 30 as part of their mission to race all eight Abbott World Marathon Majors. But what sets them apart from other individual runners is that they compete together as a team. Amy has Bethlem myopathy, a rare form of muscular dystrophy, so Jamie pushes her in a racing wheelchair. They hope their story can inspire others with disabilities to chase big dreams, too.
